system_note: Billed: Readmission claim RM_10 (admit 2026-08-20) principal diagnosis T81.4XXA (Infection following a procedure). Guideline gate: Lake Ontario Health Cooperative review window = 30 days from prior discharge; gap_days = 5, so this readmission is in-scope (Policy: Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline, Review Window = "30 days from prior discharge") (Policy document, position 4). Clinical evidence: the readmission discharge summary explicitly documents a post-sternotomy deep sternal wound infection/mediastinitis with MSSA bacteremia and states this is a "direct infectious complication of the CABG sternotomy from the index admission" (DISCHARGE SUMMARY, Transfer / Discharge Summary › Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 135-136). The wound assessment documents an open mediastinal wound with VAC in place and MSSA wound/blood cultures, consistent with a surgical-site/mediastinal infection arising from the index CABG (DISCHARGE SUMMARY, Transfer / Discharge Summary › Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 135-136). Policy criteria: the Lake Ontario guideline lists an "infection, bleeding event, or other complication arising from care provided during the prior stay" and separately lists "complication of a surgical procedure performed during the prior stay (for example, wound infection, dehiscence...)" as Finding criteria (Policy document, positions 13 and 14). No exclusion in Section C applies to this case. Reasoned determination: documentation meets the guideline's relatedness criteria - specifically a surgical complication (post-sternotomy mediastinitis / deep sternal wound infection) that is explicitly linked in the readmission record to the index CABG - therefore RM_10 is a Finding under the guideline's "surgical complication" / "infection or complication of care" criteria. Key citations: DISCHARGE SUMMARY (Transfer / Discharge Summary › Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 135-136): Clinical Relationship and WOUND / SURGICAL SITE ASSESSMENT; Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline (position 4: "30 days from prior discharge"; position 13: infection/complication criterion; position 14: surgical complication criterion).
rationale_letter: Re: Readmission Review Determination - Claim RM_10 Dear Provider, We completed a readmission review for patient Dmitri Voronin (Claim RM_10), admitted 08/20/2026, following index admission MR_10 (04/15/2026-08/15/2026). Lake Ontario Health Cooperative's Readmission Review Guideline (30-day review window) was used to evaluate whether the readmission was clinically related to the index stay. Determination: Finding - The readmission (RM_10) is clinically related to the index admission (MR_10) and meets the payer's readmission Finding criteria. Basis for Determination: - Policy gate: The payer's guideline applies to readmissions within 30 days of prior discharge; RM_10 occurred 5 days after MR_10 discharge and is therefore in-scope (Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline: "30 days from prior discharge"). - Clinical facts relied on from the medical record: The DISCHARGE SUMMARY for RM_10 documents a post-sternotomy deep sternal wound infection/mediastinitis (T81.4XXA) with MSSA bacteremia and explicitly states this is a "direct infectious complication of the CABG sternotomy from the index admission" (DISCHARGE SUMMARY, Transfer / Discharge Summary › Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 135-136). The same document details the sternal wound characteristics and ongoing wound VAC management, confirming an operative-site infection directly tied to the earlier CABG. - Policy criterion applied: Lake Ontario's guideline identifies both (a) "new infection ... arising from care provided during the prior stay" and (b) "complication of a surgical procedure performed during the prior stay (for example, wound infection...)" as Finding criteria. The readmission documentation satisfies these criteria by identifying a post-sternotomy mediastinitis that arose from the index CABG. Correction: Per Lake Ontario Health Cooperative's Readmission Review Guideline, the readmission RM_10 is a related readmission (surgical-site infection/mediastinitis) and will be addressed per the payer's claims adjudication rules for related readmissions (i.e., treated as a related complication of index admission MR_10). If you believe additional documentation would affect this determination, please submit it for reconsideration and cite the claim number RM_10. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team Lake Ontario Health Cooperative Review

evidence_cited.excerpt: WOUND / SURGICAL SITE ASSESSMENT AT DISCHARGE Deep sternal wound (mediastinitis following CABG at index admission MR_10): Sternal wound VAC in place (125 mmHg continuous). Wound dimensions: approximately 8x4 cm open mediastinal wound. Wound bed: 70% red granulation tissue, 30% yellow fibrinous base. Sternal wires visible at wound base; sternal bone stable, no dehiscence of distal wire cerclage. Surrounding skin: mild erythema, no crepitus, no fluctuance. No active purulent drainage at discharge (previously 60-80 mL/24h; now <30 mL/24h). VAC changed Day 10. Cardiothoracic surgery following; next VAC change at SNF on Day 14.
